chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Loft nightclub, Mummers Club, Cat's Meow and Chapman night
summary: Whaley retells playing the loft club with singer Mary Strange, Jack Legs Diamond, a holdup, the Cat's Meow and the Prisoner's Song.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Uh huh. Now go on with the story.
Where was I?
You were talking about Lucky Roberts and how you got started when you went off by yourself.

Right. I started playing around these clubs, see, to get a job, and we went down on the -- on Broadway there, 1800 block, in there, between 56th and 57th Street. Or 55th and 56th Street, there's a big building there, and it was a loft, see, and they had a nightclub up there and I got a job there, and they used to have colored singers, Mary Strange was one of them --
Mary Strange?
Mary Strange, yes.
That's a wild name.
Yeah, and she could sing -- she knew a whole lot of songs, see, and she could entertain and pull her dress up and put it on the table and take a dollar bill off the table.
How do they do that? They put their legs up there and ...
Just go up there and put that dollar bill up there and take their what's it's name and bring it on back.
Yeah!
So they pulled the colored singers out and put whites in there. Now the colored singers

used to give us 50¢ -- if they got a dollar, they'd give us 50¢ of it. So the white singers came in and they gave us 10¢ on the dollar, so I told Harry, the boss, I said, "Say, you know what? The colored singers gave us 50¢ on the dollar, you know, they get a dollar and they give us 50¢, and now these people only give us 10¢ -- I can't make no money playing for them for 10¢" and he said, "Well, I can't do nothing about it" and I said, "Well, I'm quitting."

It was on a Saturday night, and I quit. Monday morning, they had another band in there and they got raided, they got shot up. The gangsters shot the place up, and that's where Jack "Legs" Diamond used to come in, and he used to sit way down there and tell the waiter to tell the piano player to tell so and so to play so and so.

And he never sent up any money. So I called Harry and I said, do you see that guy sitting way down there with Jack "Legs" Diamond, he always wore a derby. the derby on? ^ I said, "now he's been sitting up here every night asking for different songs and he never sends any money back," and he said, "Well, that's Legs Diamond" -- yeah, and then we went down, I got another job down on 33rd Street, the Mummers Club.
Huh? I never heard of that, the Mummers Club.
Mummer's Club, yeah, played down there, and the gangsters come in there one Saturday night and I'd see

all these guys coming in and I said to I don't know who was playing with me, but I remember I said, "Harry, who let these guys in?" I had one of them say that to the guy and he said, "Keep on playing, and jump on the chair" and he got a gun, and they were all -- everybody -- and after we closed up and went up to Small's --
That's Harlem.
Yeah, on 135th Street.
That was bad.
Yeah. And there were those gangsters, and they said, "Well, we have to get money and send up to Sing Sing every so often, that's the only way we could get money".
And then I'll tell you about the band I used to play all around, and I went over to the Cat's Meow in Brooklyn.
That's a club?

That's a nightclub, yeah, where they used to have a show, and we played there, and the boss didn't pay me one week, so I went in the next week looking for my money and he didn't give me any money, so I quit. I told the fellows, don't play no music. He wants some music, let him pay us.
So that fizzled out. Then I went up to Harlem there to 132nd Street down at the end, they had a club there, and this was during the time that Gerald Chapman was caught up
there in Connecticut, and he was electrocuted, and they tried to buy him off, and I never seen so many thousand dollar bills and hundred dollar bills in my life that come up.

So they couldn't buy it off, see, so when he was electrocuted, all I did was play 'The Prisoner's Song.' Da, da, da, da ... The boss said to play 'The Prisoner's Song' all night long, and that's all I played.
